title: Quarterly Roadmap Harmonization: Hosted API Model Cohorts & Surge Policy
creator: Asha Patel
project: Hosted API + Model Catalog Q2 Alignment
description: Objective: Produce a coordinated quarterly roadmap that aligns Hosted API endpoint commitments with the model catalog cohorting strategy and a documented surge/fallback policy. Problem: Product, Engine, and Operations teams currently plan model rotations and capacity hedges in parallel which creates mismatched canary windows, surprise capacity pressure, and downstream billing variance for customers. Scope: 1) Define model cohort tiers (Cohort A/B/C) with explicit upgrade/rotation windows and rollback criteria. 2) Produce a capacity hedging policy tied to cohort classes (reserved burst lanes, soft caps). 3) Create a canary schedule template and contingency playbook for rapid substitution of model variants. 4) Surface roadmap commitments in the console and the public Hosted API status page. Success metrics: - Reduce unexpected model substitutions during the quarter by >=60% - Keep canary failure-to-rollback time under 30 minutes in >=90% of canaries - Reduce per-token cost variance (hosted) month-over-month by <=5% due to rotation cadence
acceptance_criteria: A public-facing calendar artifact (Confluence) that lists cohort windows and model freeze dates for the quarter
A capacity-hedge runbook that SRE/Operations can execute (playbook with runbook steps and escalation)
Console UI row for 'Upcoming Model Rotations' that is gated behind feature flag and demoable
A documented rollback and substitution decision tree with owners and SLA commitments
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng (runtime), Ops, Security, and Sales engaged with the plan
updates: 2026-03-01 - Asha P: Ticket created after cross-functional kickoff. Initial draft of cohort definitions attached to Confluence. Asked ENG and SRE for capacity hedging inputs.

2026-03-03 - Jonah R: Met with Runtime leads (Priya, Markus). Runtime prefers 2-week canary windows for Cohort A but flagged KV-cache invalidation risk for large states. Planned follow-up to quantify median KV-cache size by model.

2026-03-05 - Nora (SRE) comment: Suggested adding a 'graceful-degrade' fallback lane to avoid full rollback on transient infra pressure. Proposed metrics: queue depth and tail-latency thresholds as triggers.

2026-03-09 - Design sync (Elena): Proposed a compact console card prototype to show next rotation and expected impact on latency/cost. Design PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1827
2026-03-10 - Jonah R: Consolidated decisions and submitted draft roadmap calendar for stakeholder review. Action: schedule exec review 2026-03-16.
decisions: Adopt 3 cohort tiers (A: high-signal verified, B: validated experimental, C: canary-only) for Q2 rotations
Use 2-week canary windows by default for Cohort A rotations; 1-week for Cohort B; ad-hoc gated for Cohort C
Capacity hedging will rely on a two-component model: reserved soft cap (monthly reserved capacity) + short-lived burst vouchers (SRE-controlled)
Console visibility will be behind a feature flag; initial rollout to pilot customers in Week 2 of Q2 before broad announcement
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache invalidation on model swap causes elevated latency spikes. Mitigation: run a pre-swap KV footprint audit and schedule swaps during low-traffic windows; add a fast-path cache warmup job
Risk: Bursting to reserved capacity may increase unit costs. Mitigation: build cost-estimate dashboard and require finance sign-off for burst voucher issuance over threshold

Risk: Poorly defined rollback criteria leading to slow decision-making. Mitigation: decision tree with binary triggers (error-rate > X, p95 latency > Y, model-quality drift on eval set) and named on-call owners
Risk: Customer confusion about model rotation effects on outputs. Mitigation: prepare customer-facing comms templates and a changelog entry for all Cohort A rotations
